content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper evaluates generative models for reconstruction tasks in terms of their adversarial robustness. The proposed two attack frameworks mislead the targeted generative model for reconstruction tasks.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength
1. The paper is clear, and I had no trouble understanding it.
2. The paper is well organized.

Weaknesses
1. It is not meaningful to study adversarial samples and adversarial robustness in the case of generative model-based reconstruction tasks. The attackers seem to have no motivation to attack simple generative model-based reconstruction models. The contributions to  adversarial robustness are not significant.
2. Another weakness of the paper is the lack of novelty.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper suggests a new adversarial attack method against generative models for the input reconstruction task. Unlike the existing methods (based on direct optimizations of a specific loss term), the authors provide GAN-based frameworks. These frameworks are based on training a discriminator (ensuring the reconstructed image lies on the input distribution) and a generator (generating adversarial perturbation so that the classification of the reconstructed image is changed.) The performances of both frameworks are compared to the existing attack method (that is optimization based) with two different optimizations, namely, FGSM and PGD. Some additional studies, e.g., ablation study, and latent space analysis, are provided through experiments.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
[[Strengths]]
1. The paper designs a new GAN-based framework to attack existing generative models for the input reconstruction task.
2. The experimental results show improvements compared to the competing algorithm (Pope et al., 2020).

[[Weaknesses]]
1. While generative models are widely used in practical applications, the authors set input reconstruction as a target application. However, the practical usage of input reconstruction is unclear. The authors should describe how attacking input reconstruction can be a potential threat or the need for the target application choice; for example, compared to other target applications, input reconstruction is easier to make quantitative evaluations.
2. Also, because input reconstruction cannot represent all the applications of generative models, the title is a bit misleading. Just changing the title would be an easy option. The authors may design a general framework that applies to most generative models, then specialize the framework to the input reconstruction task. (However, it looks like one of the loss terms, i.e., $L_{MSE}$, is very specific to the input reconstruction task.)
3. In the related works, the authors introduced several adversarial example attacks on generative models and pointed out that all the attacks are optimization-based attacks. However, the only attack model they compared was Pope et al., with FGSM and PGD as optimization methods. Why is the CW attack not tried, whereas it is mentioned in the related works? Using FGSM for Pope et al. might sound redundant, considering that PGD generalizes FGSM and is more powerful than FGSM. (However, I suggest keeping the FGSM version as the weakest version of possible attacks.) I recommend the authors run more experiments with more attack variants.
4. The evaluation should be made on more datasets. MNIST and the Yale Face dataset are both grayscale images and might not have enough variation to represent the real-world situation. MNIST is one of the easiest datasets to generate adversarial examples, and the cropped face images don’t seem to show enough variations to represent real-world images. For example, I’m curious whether the same method would succeed on a dataset showing different objects, e.g., CIFAR10, Traffic signs, and the reconstructed images after the attack.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The authors’ contributions look novel, and the writing is straightforward and understandable.
content.summary_of_the_review:
Attacking generative models is not explored extensively yet, and this work provides a new attack framework. Also, the suggested attack showed impressive improvement compared to existing work by Pope et al.

However, I would reject this paper for two reasons.
1. The suggested attack framework is specific to the input reconstruction task, which does not represent the entire generative model applications. 
2. The scope of experiments is not comprehensive enough regarding attack variations and the datasets. For the details, see the Weaknesses described above.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper focuses on the robustness of generative models, specifically, conditional generative adversarial networks. This work proposes two attack methods against such generative models, a standard generative attack method and a universal attack method. The effectiveness of the proposed attack is evaluated on MNIST and CYFD datasets.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
1. As pointed out by the author, the robustness of generative models is under-explored in the community. The work makes further exploration in this direction.
2. Both sample-specific adversarial perturbation and universal adversarial perturbation are considered in this study.

Weakness:
1. The overall presentation remains to be improved. The paper starts with the title ‘Evaluating Robustness of Generative Models with Adversarial Networks’. The main contributions are two frameworks in the main text. Essentially, the contributions of this work are two types of attack methods.
2. The author evaluates the generative model G with a classifier C. The accuracy of C indicates the robustness of G. However, G+C can be seen as a new classifier C’. The overall pipeline becomes a classification model again. This is nothing but a classifier with a generative model-based preprocessing.
3. The attack methods are not novel at all. Applying GAN to generate adversarial robustness has already been done in the community [1,2]. Since the whole pipeline can be seen as a classifier, the attack methods are not novel at all.
4. It is great that the author does the analysis of how the latent spaces changes when adversarial examples are fed. However, the analysis is not solid enough. Only two toy datasets are used and some results are even different. The experiments are not convincing.

[1] Lin, Zilong, Yong Shi, and Zhi Xue. "Idsgan: Generative adversarial networks for attack generation against intrusion detection." Pacific-Asia Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining. Springer, Cham, 2022.
[2] Hayes, Jamie, and George Danezis. "Learning universal adversarial perturbations with generative models." 2018 IEEE Security and Privacy Workshops (SPW). IEEE, 2018.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: Overall, the novelty is limited if the overall pipeline (generative model + classifier) is treated as a classifier. The contributions should be further clarified.
content.summary_of_the_review: Given the weakness listed above, I recommend to reject this paper.

content.title: Evaluating Robustness of Generative Models with Adversarial Networks
content.abstract: With the advent of adversarial robustness as a research area, much novel work attempts to design creative defense mechanisms against adversarial vulnerabilities that arise. While classification models are the most common target of adversarial robustness research, generative models are often underestimated though they play essential roles in many applications. This work evaluates generative models for reconstruction tasks in terms of their adversarial robustness. We constructed two frameworks: a standard and a universal-attack framework. The standard framework requires an input to find its perturbation, and the universal-attack framework generates adversarial perturbation from the distribution of a dataset. Extensive experimental evidence discussed in this paper suggests that both frameworks can effectively alter how images are reconstructed and classified using classic generative models trained on MNIST and Cropped Yale Face datasets. Further, these frameworks outperform state-of-the-art adversarial attacks. Moreover, we showcase using the proposed framework to retrain a generative model to improve its resilience against adversarial perturbations. Furthermore, for the sake of generative models, an attack may desire not to alter the latent space. Thus, we also include the analysis of the latent space.
